subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Census Privacy Paradox
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Census Privacy Paradox usable.

hook.text: The census asks your race, income, and household size. It promises confidentiality. History says otherwise.

buildup.text: Census data is protected by law: individual responses must stay confidential for 72 years.

discovery.text: But census data was used to intern Japanese Americans in WWII and to target Arab Americans after 9/11.

twist.text: The Census Bureau shared statistical information with the Department of Homeland Security in 2002 and 2003.

climax.text: The government asks for your most personal data and promises to protect it. The promise has been broken before.

punchline.text: Protected by law. Broken by the same government.

quiz.question: How was census data misused after 9/11?
options: Statistical information was shared with the Department of Homeland Security
It was sold to private companies
